standard_prerequisites.name: For a Noetherian ring the derived completion of a complex is the derived limit of the complexes tensored with the quotients by the powers of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the object whose cohomology is being computed with the derived limit of the systems appearing in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: The cohomology of the derived completion of a pseudo-coherent complex is the inverse limit of the cohomology of the quotients
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes the cohomology of the derived completion as the inverse limit of the cohomology of the powers, which is the left hand side of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: A short exact sequence of inverse systems gives a short exact sequence relating the derived limit and the inverse limit, with the obstruction term on the left
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the displayed short exact sequence whose middle term is the computed cohomology and whose right hand term is the limit in the statement.

core_obligations: Recall that the derived completion of K is the derived limit of the complexes K tensored with the quotients by the powers of the ideal, referring to the author's Noetherian comparison statement (proof lines 28538-28540).

Use the pseudo-coherence statement to identify the cohomology of that derived completion with the inverse limit of the cohomology of the quotients, which is the left hand side of the asserted equality (proof lines 28541-28542).

Apply the breaking of a long exact sequence of modules to the relevant short exact sequence of systems, obtaining the displayed four term exact sequence with the first derived limit of the shifted cohomology on the left (proof lines 28543-28547).
Conclude from the Mittag-Leffler hypothesis that the first derived limit vanishes, so the middle term equals the right hand term and the two limits in the statement agree (proof lines 28548-28550).
proof_roadmap: Identify the derived completion as the derived limit of the quotients (proof lines 28538-28540).
Compute its cohomology as the inverse limit of the cohomology of the quotients (proof lines 28541-28542).
Write down the exact sequence relating the two limits (proof lines 28543-28547).
Kill the obstruction term with Mittag-Leffler and read off the equality (proof lines 28548-28550).
